# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I can feel no distinguishing tactile features yet; the wire positions are available but nothing identifies which to cut. Mute has the manual and Deaf can see the bomb, so they must establish the procedure visually and have Deaf relay the resulting wire number aloud to me.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I can feel no distinguishing features. Please communicate the manual's procedure to Deaf by gesture; Deaf should then say aloud which wire position I must cut.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "🤚"])
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

No information has arrived. The useful route is Deaf describing all visible markings aloud on the next turn, so Mute and I can hear; Mute can then apply the manual and communicate the required wire choice to Deaf with an agreed gesture code.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please ask Deaf by gesture to describe every visible display, light, wire colour, and marking aloud. After hearing it, use a clear counted finger gesture to tell Deaf the wire number to instruct me to cut.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "🫱", "🫲", "✍"])
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Bomb view: display zero. Light is yellow. Wires, left to right: position one yellow, position two red, position three green.

Deaf’s report gives the visible state: display 0, yellow light, and yellow/red/green wires in positions 1/2/3. Mute also heard that report and can use the manual. Since Mute cannot speak to me, I will use Deaf as relay: Mute should signal the selected position by repeating one gesture exactly once, twice, or three times; Deaf can count it and say the corresponding wire number aloud.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Visible state is display 0, yellow light; wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. Apply the manual. Signal Deaf the chosen position by gesturing ☝ repeated exactly that many times: once=wire 1, twice=wire 2, three times=wire 3. Deaf, please say the count aloud to me.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝", "☝"])
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: light is now red. Display remains zero. Wires remain 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green.

The updated visible state is display 0, red light, with wires yellow/red/green in positions 1/2/3. Mute must use the manual’s instruction for that state. I will ask Mute to send the resulting wire number as a repeated gesture; Deaf can observe and report the number aloud.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Current state: display 0, light red, wires 1 yellow 2 red 3 green. Apply the manual. Send Deaf ☝ once for wire 1, twice for wire 2, or three times for wire 3; Deaf, report the number aloud.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝", "☝"])
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: light is green. Display zero. Wires unchanged: one yellow, two red, three green.

The light has changed again, now green; display remains 0 and wire positions remain yellow/red/green. No wire instruction has been relayed. The numeric gesture convention is already stated in speech to Mute and Deaf, so Mute can now give Deaf the manual-derived choice directly, and Deaf can speak its count to me.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Current state: display 0; green light; wire positions 1=yellow, 2=red, 3=green. Please apply the manual now and gesture to Deaf ☝ once (cut 1), twice (cut 2), or three times (cut 3).")
speak(to="deaf", text="When Mute makes one, two, or three ☝ gestures this round, please immediately tell me aloud: cut wire 1, 2, or 3 respectively.")
wait()
```

ACTION BOARD:

LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: light is white. Display zero. Wires: one yellow, two red, three green.

The previous turn had no effect because it included an invalid gesture symbol. The current reported state remains display 0, white light, with wire positions 1 yellow, 2 red, and 3 green. I will restate the manual request to Mute and use only valid gesture-alphabet symbols to prompt Deaf to attend to Mute’s counted index-finger signal.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Current state: display 0, WHITE light; wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. Use the manual. Tell Deaf the selected wire with ☝ once for wire 1, twice for wire 2, or three times for wire 3.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "☝", "☝", "☝"])
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Current bomb view: orange light, display zero, wire one yellow, wire two red, wire three green.

The bomb’s visible state is now display 0 with an orange light and wires 1 yellow, 2 red, and 3 green. Mute has heard the state reports and must apply the manual; no decision has yet been relayed. I will make the relay code unambiguous using three distinct valid gestures rather than repetition: thumbs-up means wire 1, thumbs-down means wire 2, and OK means wire 3. Deaf can observe Mute’s gesture and say the result aloud.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="For the current state—display 0, orange light, wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green—use the manual and gesture your answer to Deaf: thumbs-up means cut wire 1; thumbs-down means cut wire 2; OK sign means cut wire 3.")
speak(to="deaf", text="Please watch Mute's next answer gesture and tell me aloud: thumbs-up is wire 1, thumbs-down is wire 2, OK sign is wire 3.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "👎", "👌"])
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: Nobody could receive that, so your speak reached nobody.
Deaf says: Update: light is blue. Display zero. Wires unchanged: one yellow, two red, three green.

The blue-light state has reached Mute through Deaf’s spoken update. My attempted spoken instruction to Deaf cannot work, because Deaf cannot hear me; only gesture can reach Deaf. I will use an intuitive visual relay: Mute should point left for wire 1, straight ahead for the middle wire 2, or right for wire 3. Deaf can see both the bomb’s left-to-right layout and Mute’s pointing gesture, then speak the selected position to me.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Current state: display 0, BLUE light; wires left-to-right are 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. Apply the manual. Tell Deaf your answer visually: gesture 👈 for wire 1 (left), 🫵 for wire 2 (middle), or 👉 for wire 3 (right).")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👈", "🫵", "👉"])
wait()
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: light is purple again. Display zero. Wires are one yellow, two red, three green.

The current visual state reported by Deaf is display 0, purple light, and wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. We still have no manual-derived choice from Mute. I will give Mute a fixed visual code to send Deaf and show Deaf the same number-to-position pairing: one finger plus left means wire 1, two fingers plus middle means wire 2, and three fingers plus right means wire 3. Deaf can then speak the selected number to me.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Current state: display 0, PURPLE light; wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. Apply the manual and signal Deaf exactly one pair: ☝ then 👈 means cut wire 1; ✌ then 🫵 means cut wire 2; 🤟 then 👉 means cut wire 3.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👈", "✌", "🫵", "🤟", "👉"])
wait()
```

ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: light is yellow. Display zero. Wires remain one yellow, two red, three green. Observed light cycle so far repeats purple, yellow, red, green, white, orange, blue.

The repeating cycle is now known: purple, yellow, red, green, white, orange, blue. At the current yellow state, Mute has only just received my previous request at the start of the next round; Mute can signal the manual’s answer to Deaf before Deaf’s next report. I will keep the simple left/middle/right gesture code.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="At your next turn, apply the manual to the current state and gesture only one answer for Deaf: 👈 = cut wire 1, 🫵 = cut wire 2, 👉 = cut wire 3.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👈", "🫵", "👉"])
wait()
```

ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]

WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Current view: red light, display zero, wires one yellow, two red, three green. Mute’s last visible signal to me was one raised index finger; no explicit action word was available.

Mute’s observed one raised index finger matches the established count code for wire 1. Deaf has confirmed that Mute made this signal after receiving the manual request. I will cut wire 1.

```text
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
